reasons: The document genuinely lacks any insurance covenant (no CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp or certificate requirement), and this is a hosting/data-processing engagement (Kubient stores visitor data per Section 9(b)(iii)), so the 'missing' classification is correct and falls within the rule's walk-away zone rather than the fallback.

The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook model language closely (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where Customer/visitor data is processed, workers' comp as required by Law, certificates on request, term plus one year) and is placed in the General Provisions section as the redline guidance directs, with no alteration of existing text.
The comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, cites the playbook position and offers a negotiation fallback on limits; deterministic checks confirm the insurance obligation is present.
Minor, non-blocking nit: the inserted text is appended after subsection (i) without an explicit '(j)' subsection label referenced in the rationale — a formatting cleanup, not a substantive defect.
